scope: Source-derived standalone corrected GDN normalization, separate Q/K RMS_NORM then SCALE versus a fused launch. Not a compiled full-backend comparison, provider qualification, or end-to-end inference speed measurement.

baseline.description: Four launches: Q RMS, Q SCALE, K RMS, K SCALE. RMS uses 256 threads per 128-wide row and the source reduction order; SCALE retains factor*x + positive-zero bias.

candidate.description: One launch with separate Q/K blocks and unchanged 256-thread row reduction topology. Volatile F32 normalized intermediate preserves former RMS-store rounding before SCALE.

dependency_observations.note: calling-init paths are a bounded observation from compile diagnostics, not every loader record or a complete dependency attestation. Six ELF dependencies match the prior one-wave fixture; no RPATH/RUNPATH.

analysis.sample_units: microseconds per provider call over both Q and K; HIP events bracket a batch of 100 calls (direct) or one captured graph containing 100 calls (graph), divided by 100
analysis.median_definition: Mean of sorted samples at zero-based indices 9 and 10, separately for each provider, shape, mode and trial.
analysis.ratio_definition: baseline_median_us / candidate_median_us; greater than 1 means lower candidate median. Ratios of medians, not medians of paired ratios.
verification: Actual compile and run output sizes and SHA-256 hashes verified, including both complete prefix evidence files for every phase.
All phases process-complete with no process failure; canonical prefix hashes match before/after with physical and semantic equality.
Both runs use the exact reviewed compiled binary, diagnostics disabled, empty stderr, passing GPU preflight and acquired GPU lease held through receipt, released with matching phase hash.
Exact bitwise baseline/candidate equality and independent float64 corrected-formula diagnostic oracle passed before and after each timing mode; output/scratch guards and full input bytes checked.
Zero/signed-zero, near-epsilon, tiny, large and mixed finite inputs with two sequences and unequal Q/K epsilon passed both diagnostic sweeps.
All 480 raw samples positive and finite; all 24 medians independently recomputed and 12 ratios calculated separately.
All measurement metadata, input/output hashes, device identity, loader paths and correctness reports match between the two processes; loader path list matches the previous one-wave run.
limitations: Only width128,16Q/Kheads,tokens1/16/512,one sequence are timed. Synthetic two-sequence diagnostics use three tokens. No claim for all shapes, layouts, epsilon values or finite magnitudes.
Float64 tolerances atol2e-7 and rtol2e-5 are diagnostic acceptance thresholds, not a proof of rsqrt accuracy or an all-finite-input error bound. Exact GPU parity is separately required.
The baseline is a source-derived arithmetic extraction, not the compiled current Halo backend. Shared implementation components and compiler behavior remain part of the experiment.
Captured graphs contain 100 repetitions on fixed inputs and addresses. They are not llama token graphs and omit inter-operation dependencies, changing activations and recurrent-state traffic.
No confidence intervals, significance claim or pooling of trials/modes. Fixed shape/mode order and uncontrolled clocks/power or other GPU clients can affect timings.

The GPU lease serializes cooperating jobs only. HIP event timing includes stream work and possible enqueue gaps; validation, transfers, allocation, capture and instantiation are outside measured intervals.
No integration patch or end-to-end token/logit/continuation comparison was measured. These ratios cannot be converted into inference speedup.
Metadata coverage remains unknown and vendor authenticity unverified. External host-library hash snapshots reported by root are not independently certified here.
Receipt hashes locate retained external evidence; binaries and large prefix inventories are not embedded.
